materials.title: README planning worksheet
materials.description: Plan the minimum sections needed to help users understand, use, and contribute to the project.
materials.disclaimer: This worksheet is an editable starting point. Replace every bracketed prompt and remove sections that do not apply. Do not claim features, support, or compliance that has not been verified.
materials.content:
# [Project name]

## What this project does
[Describe the user problem and the software's purpose in plain language.]

## Who it helps
[Describe the intended users or contributors.]

## Current status
[State the current release, stability, and important limitations.]

## Use the software
[Provide the shortest safe path to use or run the project.]

## Local development
[Add setup, test, and validation commands.]

## Contributing
[Link CONTRIBUTING.md and beginner-friendly issues.]

## Accessibility
[Link the accessibility statement and reporting process.]

## Security
[Link SECURITY.md. Do not place sensitive vulnerability details in public issues.]

## Support
[Link SUPPORT.md and state realistic response expectations.]

## License
[Name and link the open-source license.]

materials.title: Accessibility statement starter
materials.description: Draft an honest accessibility commitment, testing summary, limitation list, and reporting process.
materials.disclaimer: This starter does not establish WCAG conformance or accessibility certification. Report only testing that was actually completed and keep known limitations visible.
materials.content:
# Accessibility

## Commitment
[State the project's accessibility goal in plain language.]

## Current support
[List the browsers, devices, keyboard use, and assistive technologies actually tested.]

## Automated checks
[List automated tools and what they can and cannot verify.]

## Manual testing
[List completed keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, reflow, contrast, motion, touch, and device checks.]

## Known limitations
- [Limitation, affected task, and available workaround]

## Report an accessibility barrier
[Provide an accessible public or private reporting route.]

Include the affected task, browser, operating system, assistive technology when relevant, expected behavior, actual behavior, and whether the barrier blocks a core task.

Do not include passwords, access tokens, confidential reports, or unnecessary personal information.

## Response and prioritization
[Explain realistic acknowledgement expectations and how blocking barriers are prioritized.]

materials.title: Security policy review worksheet
materials.description: Review whether the security policy gives reporters a safe, realistic, project-specific process.
materials.disclaimer: This worksheet is general project guidance, not a security assessment or guarantee that the software is secure.
materials.content:
# Security policy review

- [ ] Supported versions are stated.
- [ ] A monitored private reporting route is provided.
- [ ] Public exploit disclosure is discouraged until coordination is complete.
- [ ] Reporters are asked for reproduction, impact, and environment details.
- [ ] The policy does not request passwords, tokens, or unnecessary personal data.
- [ ] Project-specific in-scope and out-of-scope examples are included.
- [ ] A realistic acknowledgement target is stated.
- [ ] Severity and prioritization are explained.
- [ ] Remediation, verification, and coordinated disclosure are described.
- [ ] Threat-model and incident-response documents are linked.
- [ ] The policy avoids claiming that a file or score proves security.

## Next actions
- Owner: [name or team]
- Target review date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Highest-priority gap: [describe]

materials.title: Threat model outline
materials.description: Create a lightweight review of assets, trust boundaries, misuse cases, mitigations, and remaining risk.
materials.disclaimer: A threat model helps prioritize risk; it does not prove that threats are eliminated or that the project is secure.
materials.content:
# Threat model

## Scope and architecture
[Describe the software, data flow, deployment, and important exclusions.]

## Assets
- [Asset and why it matters]

## Trust boundaries
- [Boundary, data or permission crossing it, and who controls each side]

## Misuse cases
| Misuse case | Likely impact | Existing mitigation | Residual risk | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Example] | [Impact] | [Mitigation] | [Remaining risk] | [Owner] |

## Repository and supply-chain risks
[Review dependencies, automation actions, permissions, releases, and deployment integrity.]

## Review triggers
- Architecture change
- New data type or import path
- New dependency or automation permission
- Security incident
- Maintainer or service-access change

## Follow-up issues
- [Issue link and priority]

materials.title: Incident-response checklist
materials.description: Prepare an ordered, adaptable process for receiving, containing, fixing, verifying, and communicating an incident.
materials.disclaimer: This checklist is a planning aid, not a managed incident-response service. Adapt roles and steps to the project's real architecture and capacity.
materials.content:
# Security incident-response checklist

## 1. Receive and protect the report
- [ ] Confirm the private channel.
- [ ] Limit access to people needed for response.
- [ ] Record time, reporter contact, affected versions, and evidence.

## 2. Triage
- [ ] Confirm the issue or document uncertainty.
- [ ] Assess impact, exploitability, exposure, and affected users.
- [ ] Assign decision authority and an incident owner.

## 3. Contain
- [ ] Reduce ongoing exposure.
- [ ] Protect logs and evidence.
- [ ] Avoid unverified public statements.

## 4. Remediate and verify
- [ ] Prepare the smallest safe fix.
- [ ] Add regression tests.
- [ ] Review accessibility and compatibility impact.
- [ ] Verify the release and deployment artifact.

## 5. Communicate
- [ ] Coordinate disclosure with the reporter when possible.
- [ ] Publish user actions and affected versions when necessary.
- [ ] Avoid exposing secrets or unnecessary personal data.

## 6. Learn
- [ ] Record lessons learned.
- [ ] Update the threat model, policy, tests, and follow-up issues.

materials.title: Governance roles worksheet
materials.description: Define current roles, decision authority, repository permissions, conflicts, and continuity.
materials.disclaimer: Use only roles and contacts that exist or have explicitly agreed to serve. Do not invent an independent reviewer or successor.
materials.content:

[Example: maintainer-led project with public discussion for significant changes.]

materials.title: Support boundaries starter
materials.description: Set realistic channels, response expectations, scope boundaries, and maintainer-availability rules.
materials.disclaimer: Do not promise response times or services the project cannot reliably provide. This starter does not create paid or guaranteed support.
materials.content:
# Support

## Supported requests
- Reproducible software defects
- Documentation questions
- Focused feature proposals
- Accessibility barriers through the documented route

## Separate confidential routes
- Security concerns: [link SECURITY.md]
- Code of Conduct reports: [link CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md]

## Response expectations
[State a realistic best-effort acknowledgement target.]

Opening an issue does not guarantee implementation, a specific timeline, or individual troubleshooting.

## Out of scope
- [List project-specific exclusions]
- Requests requiring private credentials or confidential data
- Unrelated commercial, consulting, implementation, or hosting services

## Triage outcomes
Accepted, needs information, duplicate, deferred, out of scope, or closed after inactivity.

## Maintainer availability
[Explain pauses, reduced availability, and how urgent confidential reports are handled.]

materials.title: Conduct enforcement worksheet
materials.description: Review report intake, conflicts, privacy, proportional consequences, anti-retaliation, and reconsideration.
materials.disclaimer: This worksheet is a process starter. Do not name a secondary contact, reviewer, or enforcement team without explicit consent.
materials.content:
# Code of Conduct enforcement review

- [ ] Scope covers repository and community spaces.
- [ ] Unacceptable behavior has practical examples.
- [ ] A private reporting route is monitored.
- [ ] Reports involving the normal recipient have a conflict-safe process.
- [ ] Access to reports is limited.
- [ ] Evidence, confidentiality, and record handling are described.
- [ ] A realistic acknowledgement expectation is stated.
- [ ] Enforcement options are proportionate.
- [ ] Anti-retaliation protection is included.
- [ ] Unsubstantiated reports are distinguished from knowingly false reports.
- [ ] Outcome communication and one-time reconsideration are described.
- [ ] Platform escalation is available for urgent safety risks.

## Current gaps
- [Gap, owner, and next action]

materials.title: Privacy-respecting metrics plan
materials.description: Choose a small set of measurements connected to decisions, community health, and maintainer capacity.
materials.disclaimer: Metrics are context, not certification. Popularity measures such as stars or views should not be presented as proof of project health.
materials.content:
# Project-health metrics plan

## Goals
- [Goal the project is trying to support]

## Measures
| Metric | Why it matters | Source | Review cadence | Decision supported |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Issue acknowledgement time | [Reason] | GitHub issues | Monthly | [Decision] |
| Open issue and pull-request load | [Reason] | GitHub | Monthly | [Decision] |
| First-time and returning contributors | [Reason] | GitHub | Per release | [Decision] |
| Accessibility issues opened and resolved | [Reason] | GitHub | Per release | [Decision] |
| Roadmap goals completed, deferred, or cancelled | [Reason] | Roadmap | Per release | [Decision] |

## Privacy boundaries
- Do not collect checklist or project-profile data from user browsers.
- Prefer aggregate repository information.
- Do not use metrics to pressure maintainers into unhealthy activity.

## Interpretation notes
[Record important limitations and context.]

materials.title: License and third-party material review
materials.description: Review the project license, contribution terms, dependencies, automation actions, documentation, and assets.
materials.disclaimer: This worksheet provides general information and is not legal advice. Seek qualified advice for unresolved licensing questions or custom terms.
materials.content:
# License and third-party material review

## Project license
- [ ] A recognized open-source license is in the repository root.
- [ ] The README names and links the license.
- [ ] Copyright holder and year are accurate.
- [ ] License coverage for code, documentation, and project assets is understood.

## Contributions
- [ ] Contribution guidance explains that submissions follow the project license.
- [ ] No additional contributor agreement is required without a documented need.

## Third-party review
| Material | Source | License or permission | Compatibility | Attribution required | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Dependency, action, image, font, documentation, or snippet] | [Source] | [Terms] | [Review] | [Yes/No] | [Keep/replace/remove] |

## Follow-up
- [ ] Add THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md when attribution is required.
- [ ] Remove or replace material with unclear permission.
- [ ] Review new third-party material during pull requests and releases.
